question: What are the expenses of the budget with the lowest remaining?
evidence: expense of budget refers to expense_description; lowest remaining refers to MIN(remaining)
clarification: If several rows tie at the cut-off, return all of them.
gold: SELECT c0 FROM (SELECT T2.expense_description AS c0, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY T1.remaining) AS __r FROM budget AS T1 INNER JOIN expense AS T2 ON T1.budget_id = T2.link_to_budget) AS __t WHERE __r <= 1
gold0: SELECT T2.expense_description FROM budget AS T1 INNER JOIN expense AS T2 ON T1.budget_id = T2.link_to_budget ORDER BY T1.remaining LIMIT 1

c.request:
What are the expenses of the budget with the lowest remaining?
Evidence: expense of budget refers to expense_description; lowest remaining refers to MIN(remaining)
If several rows tie at the cut-off, return all of them.
c.sql: SELECT e.expense_description FROM expense e JOIN budget b ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE b.remaining = (SELECT MIN(remaining) FROM budget)

b.request: List the expense_description of every expense linked to any budget whose remaining value equals the minimum remaining across all budgets, including all expenses of every budget tied for the lowest remaining
b.sql: SELECT e.expense_description FROM expense e JOIN budget b ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE b.remaining = (SELECT MIN(remaining) FROM budget)

d.request: What are the expenses (expense_description) of the budget with the lowest remaining amount (MIN(remaining)), and if several rows tie for the lowest remaining value, return all of them?
d.sql: SELECT e.expense_description FROM expense e JOIN budget b ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE b.remaining = (SELECT MIN(remaining) FROM budget)
